content.intro: Learn http status codes and responses through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: HTTP Status Codes and Responses matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines http status codes and responses as part of django architecture and http fundamentals. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: Successful responses; Redirect responses; Client errors; Server errors; Choosing suitable status codes. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: Successful responses
items.text: Successful responses is part of the request/response contract. Match routes and methods explicitly, return an appropriate response/status, and test success, missing-resource and unauthorized paths.

items.title: Redirect responses
items.text: Redirect responses is part of the request/response contract. Match routes and methods explicitly, return an appropriate response/status, and test success, missing-resource and unauthorized paths.

items.title: Client errors
items.text: Treat Client errors as a reproducible diagnostic: capture the exact input and observed result, isolate one hypothesis, and add a regression test once the cause is fixed. Avoid exposing internal stack traces or secrets to public users.

items.title: Server errors
items.text: Treat Server errors as a reproducible diagnostic: capture the exact input and observed result, isolate one hypothesis, and add a regression test once the cause is fixed. Avoid exposing internal stack traces or secrets to public users.

items.title: Choosing suitable status codes

Use the accompanying example as a starting point, verify it with the official versioned documentation, and record one test demonstrating expected behavior.

content_blocks.text: Change one input or configuration choice related to Successful responses. Write down the expected outcome, test one normal case and one invalid or boundary case, then record what changed. Do not add real credentials or sensitive production data.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
